summary.headline: Hy-Tech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22-32% YoY to INR60.9 crores with EBITDA of INR14.5 crores at a 23.8% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR60.9 crores, up 22% YoY (management also cited 32% in its opening remarks) and up 41% QoQ. EBITDA rose 21% YoY to INR14.5 crores at a 23.8% margin, versus 19.6% in Q1, and PAT rose 23% YoY to INR8.5 crores. H1 FY27 revenue was INR103.9 crores (+18%), with EBITDA of INR22.9 crores (+14%) and PAT of INR13.1 crores (+19%). Management said a price revision agreed with customers after 7-8 years is being billed from H2, and guided FY27 PAT growth of about 18-25% (clarified as 20-22% this year and 24-25% in FY28).

financial_highlights.change: +22% YoY vs INR49.8 crores; +41% QoQ (management also cited 32% YoY in opening remarks)
vs 24% in Q2 FY26; vs 19.6% in Q1 FY27
+18% vs INR87.8 crores in H1 FY26
+19% vs INR11 crores; PAT margin 12.6%, stable

segments.name: Hydraulic fittings (core business)
segments.commentary: Management calls this the primary growth engine, with nearly 11,000 SKUs. Growth is coming from share-of-business gains at existing OEMs and new OEM onboarding. John Deere is about 12% of total turnover.

segments.name: Stainless steel double ferrule fittings (new)
segments.commentary: Development took about 2-2.5 years. Current business is INR8-10 crores, with margins about 5 percentage points higher than carbon steel. Railway and Engineers India registrations are done; results are expected in 1-2 years.

segments.name: US exports / aftermarket
segments.commentary: US business has been flat due to tariffs. A wholly-owned subsidiary and a warehouse in New Jersey were set up to supply John Deere, Caterpillar and Case New Holland. The US aftermarket is described as the bulk of demand.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 is expected to be stronger than H1. Management cited a historical split of about 45-46% of turnover in H1 and 53-55% in H2, and said H2 EBITDA margin will be about 24% or better.
Full-year FY27 PAT growth is guided at about 18-20% on the first call, clarified as 20-22% on this call. Management said FY27 revenue growth of 20% is achievable.
FY28 PAT growth is guided at about 24-25%, linked to the US tariff situation easing and new customer wins.
Management said revenue will double within 3 years and that the business could reach INR500 crores of turnover in 4-5 years using existing land and added machinery.

All price revisions are finalised and accepted by customers; the second half will be billed entirely at revised prices. About 25% of the earlier shortfall from the price change is still to be recovered.
capex_capacity: Current utilisation is about 70%, and management keeps about 20-30% free capacity for new customers as a policy.

Existing infrastructure (land and buildings) is sufficient for about INR500 crores of turnover; reaching that level requires more machinery. The new land parcel (6.5 acres at Shirwal) is for beyond INR500 crores, with a factory timeline of 2.5-3 years.
Investment is going into automated machinery, including rotary transfer machines.

INR30 crores from the IPO object is to be invested over about 1.5 years and is expected to support about INR100 crores of revenue. Management expects internally generated cash of about INR25-30 crores over 2 years to fund further capex.
demand_pricing: Order books are full: management said the company is 'completely booked' with schedules from all OEMs. Tractor demand is softening, offset by rising excavator demand.

Price revisions were agreed with customers after 7-8 years, partly due to the war situation. Management said the revision covered both raw material and conversion cost increases, and that only about 25% of the raw material pass-through had been recovered before this quarter.
Management said the company earns about a 10% price premium in the market and that MNCs such as Parker import and sell at about 2x Hy-Tech's prices.
Domestic market: the company has integrity clauses with OEMs not to sell their fittings in the domestic aftermarket. The US business is largely aftermarket through distributors.
India hydraulic fittings market: management estimated about INR2,000 crores of potential against current revenue of about INR190-200 crores. It described the market as growing about 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 growth continue, and will EBITDA margin expand? Is the 25-30% PAT growth target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 will be much better than H1, with EBITDA margin of about 24% guaranteed. H2 typically accounts for 53-55% of turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company recovered the Q1 revenue lost to the 1 April price revision?
qa_highlights.answer: Not fully. About 25% of the previous shortfall is still to be recovered, and management expects full recovery in the next half.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term growth outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PAT growth is about 20-22%, with FY28 at about 24-25%. The gap reflects flat US sales due to tariffs, which are expected to improve after the US midterm elections.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential of the current capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it runs at about 70% by policy and keeps 20% free capacity. It guided to about 25% annual growth, reaching INR500 crores in 4-5 years. The INR30 crores IPO spend is expected to support about INR100 crores of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price hike and pass-through lift gross margins back to 65%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the price revisions cover both raw material and conversion cost, so margins are being maintained. All revisions are finalised, and H2 will be billed at revised prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of John Deere and other OEM business, and what concentration risk exists?
qa_highlights.answer: About three John Deere plants are now supplying, and four have approved samples. John Deere is about 12% of turnover, with the ramp expected in FY28. Tata Hitachi and Sany are long-term, gradual contributors.

risks_watch: US tariff and midterm-election outcome: US growth has been flat, and management's FY28 growth guide depends on a recovery.
Customer concentration: John Deere is about 12% of turnover, and its ramp is still pending.
Recovery of the remaining ~25% of the Q1 price-revision shortfall, and whether H2 billing at revised prices lifts margins as expected.
Capacity and talent: growth beyond INR500 crores needs machinery, staff and a new factory 2.5-3 years away. Management cited people and structure as a constraint.
New product ramp: stainless steel double ferrule revenue is only INR8-10 crores so far, and defence, railway and oil and gas wins are still pending.
Management did not give specifics on the acquisition question and deferred it to the next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and H2 growth, but evasive on specifics: several questions were deflected or answered loosely, and the FY27/FY28 growth guidance was revised during the call. Management was cautious on US tariffs and new verticals, describing new-sector revenue as slow to build.
key_quotes: So 24% EBITDA down the line for the second half is guaranteed.
Hy-Tech is growing not for the new market but for the existing market.

Our integrated manufacturing capabilities, wide product portfolio of nearly 11,000 SKUs, and ability to deliver high-quality precision components have helped us establish ourselves as a trusted supplier to leading OEMs.

adds.what: 6.5-acre Shirwal land parcel for beyond INR500 crore turnover; factory timeline 2.5-3 years
INR30 crore IPO-funded automated machinery (incl. rotary transfer machines) supporting ~INR100 crore revenue

growth.why: Management guides ~20% FY27 revenue growth and a 24%+ H2 EBITDA margin, backed by full order books, a price revision billed from H2, ~70% utilisation with 20-30% spare capacity, and INR30 crore of automated machinery; FY27 PAT growth was cut to ~18-22% (20-22% on clarification), and the INR500 crore turnover target is 4-5 years out.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guaranteed about 24% EBITDA margin for H2 FY27 versus 19.6% in Q1 and 23.8% in Q2, with price revisions now fully billed from H2 and 25% of raw material pass-through still to recover.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is about 70% with 20-30% spare capacity by policy; INR30 crore automated machinery is planned over about 1.5 years, but the Shirwal factory is 2.5-3 years away, so only machinery-led capacity lands in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides about 20% FY27 revenue growth, H1 revenue was up 18% to INR103.9 crore, and H2 typically carries 53-55% of turnover; order books are described as completely booked.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 70%, and the INR30 crore IPO-funded machinery plus INR25-30 crore internal cash over 2 years are planned, so further machinery capex announcements are plausible.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 PAT growth guidance was cut from 18-20% to about 20-22% clarified, and FY27 revenue growth is only guided at about 20%, with no sign of upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The FY27 PAT guide was already revised during the call, the US business is flat on tariffs, and H2 needs a 53-55% turnover split to hit 20-22% PAT growth; the guidance has been inconsistent (18-20% vs 20-22%).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Stainless steel double ferrule fittings are at INR8-10 crore revenue with registrations done and results expected in 1-2 years, so a material launch impact is not yet visible in the window.

rows.label: Price revision billed from H2 FY27
rows.why: All price revisions are finalised and accepted; H2 is billed entirely at revised prices after 7-8 years, with about 25% of the earlier shortfall still to be recovered.

rows.label: John Deere ramp and US subsidiary
rows.why: About three John Deere plants are supplying and four have approved samples, with John Deere at about 12% of turnover; the ramp is expected in FY28 alongside a New Jersey warehouse.

rows.label: Order book fully booked
rows.why: Management says the company is completely booked with schedules from all OEMs, while tractor demand softens and excavator demand rises.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 margin (about 24%) and full order books, but cautious on US tariffs and new verticals; analysts pressed on the revised FY27 and FY28 PAT guidance, the Q1 price-shortfall recovery and capacity beyond INR500 crore, and management answered loosely on several points.
